title: CaesarCoder: Genesis Block Wallet Puzzle

author.name: CaesarCoder (anonymous until a PGP signed OP_RETURN on 2026-10-17)

prize.note: the jackpot started at 25,000 sats and grew because the author relayed every paid question into the escrow; 947,620 sats in 120 outputs when it was swept on 2026-10-17

target_format: P2WSH 2-of-2 wsh(sortedmulti(2, A, B)); each key from its own 12-word BIP39 seed (entropy = first 128 bits of sha256 of a cut of the raw genesis block hex) plus a two-word name passphrase, path m/48'/0'/account'/2'/<0;1>/*, account = raw value of a header field; the seed step uses non-standard PBKDF2 settings

derivation.summary: cut -b N-M of the 570-character raw block hex, tr -d '\n', sha256sum, first 32 hex digits as Ian Coleman Hex entropy, 12 words, two-word name passphrase, seed with the author's PBKDF2 settings (not standard BIP39, see README), BIP48 account key, 2-of-2 script compared with the witness program
derivation.certified_against: the BIP-173 P2WSH test vector, and a real 2-of-2 P2WSH spent in block 963629 (tx 47ded3504e855ce418e46eeca4694b55a623d1e23a8e3c83292abbcf9cee9f7a, input 0) whose revealed keys rebuild the script and hash to the spent address; private key 1 to the generator point; negative control against the escrow

difficulty_note: swept on 2026-10-17; the public hints fix everything except the exact cut, the passphrase and the PBKDF2 settings; the author published test vectors computed with the real settings on 2026-10-16 and 17, two hours before the sweep

leads.title: reproduce the author test vector e4caa034 (text 0, passphrase Test Example) to identify the PBKDF2 settings
ask the author or the solver for the write-up

sources.title: Escrow address and full on-chain dialogue
crypto.news, Bitcoin puzzle hides wallet key in Genesis Block data

third_party_material: none: the genesis block and the author's OP_RETURN messages are public chain data; press articles are linked, not reproduced
